From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-18T09:38:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production errors beginning 09:05 PT — 429s spiking

Quick triage notes (initial):

- Observed symptom: sustained 429s on /v1/pay/validate across the us-west clusters starting 09:05 PT. Error traces show immediate rejections from the per-customer safety valve in the rate-limiter.
- Root cause hypothesis: overlapping quota windows between the "sustained" and "burst" policies are being double-accounted on routed requests. Specifically, quota_window_ms currently set to 60000 (1m) for sustained and 15000 (15s) for burst, but an upstream routing policy (canary routing) is duplicating request counts across two q-keys when requests traverse the safety-valve layer. The net effect: clients hit both allotments and get rejected even though aggregate token usage should be within limits.
- Evidence: attached log snippet lines show identical request IDs counted twice across two q_keys; heap of 429s occur when the burst bucket refills but the sustained bucket remains depleted (see medisys_429-snippet.txt).

Immediate mitigations we can apply (suggested, in order):
1) Short-term (within 10–30m): Reduce sustained quota_window_ms from 60000 -> 15000 for the affected policy for Medisys only (faster recovery).
2) Short-term alternate: Temporarily increase burst_tokens from 200 -> 600 for 30 minutes to absorb spikes.
3) Medium (1–3h): Toggle the routing path to bypass the duplicate accounting path for Medisys traffic (route to primary pool only).
4) Longer (postmortem): Fix the routing-to-quota-key mapping so q_keys are unique per effective request.

I've pushed a log export to the ticket and attached a short CSV of current quota policy rows (quota_policy_export.csv). I'll stand by to run the config change under Olga's direction.

– Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

- We cannot have this recur during peak tomorrow morning.

We need an ETA for the first mitigation (config change) and we need an interim SLA concession/credit while this is unresolved. Medisys execs are asking for a short statement we can send to internal stakeholders.

Alex

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@medisys.com>, Medisys Ops <ops@medisys.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-18T13:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production errors beginning 09:05 PT — 429s spiking

Alex — here's our rapid mitigation plan and owners. We can execute most items within 2 hours; Marcus and Karthik can run the live changes and I will own customer comms.

Immediate (T+0 to 30m):
- Action A (Marcus): Reduce sustained quota_window_ms for Medisys policy from 60000 -> 15000 (expected immediate decrease in tail 429s).
- Action B (Karthik): Temporarily raise burst_tokens from 200 -> 600 for Medisys for 30 minutes.
- Action C (Marcus): Update routing to send Medisys traffic only to primary serving pool (bypass canary split).

Fallback (if A/B/C insufficient, T+30–120m):
- Route high-volume keys to a lower-capacity model to reduce token spend per request.
- Apply 10% additional concurrency headroom on us-west pools.

Customer-facing note (draft):
"We identified a misconfiguration in quota and burst controls that resulted in customers receiving rejections under sustained load. We have applied mitigations and are monitoring — our team will follow up with a detailed timeline and a compensation proposal."

Attachments: quota_policy_export.csv, medisys_perf_graphs_0218.png

Marcus/Karthik: please confirm when each step is complete and post the command logs to INF-6421. Alex: we'll send a brief update to your execs once the first mitigation is verified.

—Olga
